tested_condition: Phase1 can establish a production-ready Next.js application architecture without materializing approved page designs.
actual_outcome: A new App Router-based Next.js TypeScript scaffold was created with shared layout primitives, global styles, metadata placeholders, route placeholders, and architecture support files. No approved page design content was materialized.
passes: No pre-existing application architecture constrained the setup.
App Router route scaffold was established for all required routes.
TypeScript, lint, and Next.js configuration files were created.
Architecture remains explicitly separate from design-authority materialization.
architecture_summary: The repository now contains a minimal but production-oriented Next.js scaffold with route placeholders, shared shell components, metadata helpers, and mobile-first global styles.
rationale: App Router with TypeScript provides the cleanest forward path for later design-system materialization, metadata expansion, and page implementation while keeping Phase1 bounded to architecture.
